# Partie A
## A1

```{r}
ref <- read.table("data/auto2004_original.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
l3  <- read.table("data/auto2004_original_ligne3.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", skip = 3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sn  <- read.table("data/auto2004_sans_nom.txt", header = FALSE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(sn) <- colnames(ref)
dm  <- read.table("data/auto2004_don_manquante.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", na.strings = c("", "NA"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d99 <- read.table("data/auto2004_don_manquan_99999.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", na.strings = "99999", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

all.equal(dim(ref), dim(l3)) ; all.equal(names(ref), names(l3))
all.equal(dim(ref), dim(sn)) ; all.equal(names(ref), names(sn))
all.equal(dim(ref), dim(dm)) ; all.equal(names(ref), names(dm))
all.equal(dim(ref), dim(d99)) ; all.equal(names(ref), names(d99))
```

## A3
### a
```{r}
meteo <- read_delim(
  "data/stations_janvier2026.csv",
  delim = ";", 
  locale = locale(encoding = "latin1", decimal_mark = ","),
  na = c("", "NA", "-99", "n/a"),
  skip = 2,
  col_types = cols(date = col_date(format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
)
```

### b
```{r}
dim(meteo)
str(meteo)
colSums(is.na(meteo))
range(meteo$date)
unique(meteo$station)
```

## A4
### a
```{r}
bilan_meteo <- meteo %>%
  group_by(station) %>%
  summarise(
    temp_min_moy = mean(temp_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_max_moy = mean(temp_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    cumul_pluie = sum(pluie_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    jours_gel = sum(temp_min < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    jours_pluie = sum(pluie_mm > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
bilan_meteo
```

### b
```{r}
bilan_meteo %>% slice_max(jours_gel, n = 1)
bilan_meteo %>% slice_max(cumul_pluie, n = 1)
```

### c
```{r}
meteo %>%
  group_by(station) %>%
  slice_min(temp_min, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(station, date, temp_min)
```

## A5
```{r}
# read.csv utilise "," par défaut mais pour un fichier FR (csv2), il faut le séparateur ";"
p1 <- read.csv("data/prix_fr.csv")

# read.csv2 gère le ";", mais il manque peut-être un argument 'skip' ou l'encodage
p2 <- read.csv2("data/prix_fr.csv")

# read_csv2() gère bien les csv FR, mais l'erreur vient probablement du manque d'encodage
p3 <- read_csv2("data/prix_fr.csv", na = "n/a", skip = 1)

# Code corrigé :
p3_corrige <- read_csv2("data/prix_fr.csv", na = "n/a", skip = 1, locale(encoding = "latin1"))
p3_corrige
```

# Partie B
## B1
### a

Il y a 2 feuilles Excel (2024 et 2025) dont les tableaux commence à la cellule A4

### b
```{r}
pluie2024 <- read_excel("data/pluie_mensuelle.xlsx", sheet = "2024", range = "A4:M8") %>%
  mutate(annee = 2024)

pluie2025 <- read_excel("data/pluie_mensuelle.xlsx", sheet = "2025", range = "A4:M8") %>%
  mutate(annee = 2025)

pluie <- bind_rows(pluie2024, pluie2025)
```

### c
```{r}
pluie_annuelle <- pluie %>%
  group_by(station, annee) %>%
  summarise(cumul = sum(c_across(janv:déc), na.rm = TRUE))
pluie_annuelle
```

# Partie C
## C1
### a
```{r}
pluie_long <- pluie %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(station, annee),
    names_to = "mois",
    values_to = "mm"
  )
pluie_long
```

### b
```{r}
mois_niveaux <- setdiff(names(pluie), c("station", "annee"))

pluie_long <- pluie_long %>%
  mutate(mois = factor(mois, levels = mois_niveaux))
```

### c
```{r}
pluie_long %>%
  filter(annee == 2025) %>%
  group_by(station) %>%
  slice_max(mm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

### d
```{r}
diff_pluie <- pluie_long %>%
  filter(annee %in% c(2024, 2025)) %>%
  select(station, mois, annee, mm) %>%
  mutate(mm = as.numeric(mm)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = annee, 
    values_from = mm, 
    names_prefix = "an_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(diff = an_2025 - an_2024)

diff_pluie %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  slice_max(diff, n = 1)
```

## C2
```{r}
meteo_long <- meteo %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(temp_min, temp_max),
    names_to = "type_mesure",
    values_to = "temperature"
  )
meteo_long

amplitude_therm <- meteo_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type_mesure, values_from = temperature) %>%
  mutate(amplitude = temp_max - temp_min) %>%
  group_by(station) %>%
  summarise(amp_moyenne = mean(amplitude, na.rm = TRUE))

amplitude_therm
```

## C3
### a

```{r}
wines <- read_excel("data/wines.xlsx")

wines_long <- wines %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Wines, Soul),
    names_to = c("etape", "descripteur"),
    names_pattern = "(rest|view|shaking|tasting)(.*)",
    values_to = "note"
  )
wines_long
```

### b
```{r}
wines_moy_large <- wines_long %>%
  group_by(Wines, Soul, etape) %>%
  summarise(note_moyenne = mean(note, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = etape, values_from = note_moyenne) %>%
  select(Wines, Soul, rest, view, shaking, tasting)
wines_moy_large
```

### c
```{r}
wines_moy_large %>%
  slice_max(tasting, n = 3) %>%
  select(Wines, Soul, tasting)
```

### d
```{r}
cor(wines$Global, wines_moy_large$tasting)
```

# Partie D
## D1

```{r}
emp <- read_csv("data/employee.csv")
summary(emp)
emp
```

Parmis les problèmes on trouve :
- Plusieurs valeurs NA dont un qui se trouve dans la colonne identifiant l'employé
- Des valeurs mixtes pour Country (un coup minuscule, un coup majuscule)

## D2

```{r}
emp_propre <- emp %>%
  mutate(
    # Pays en majuscules
    Country = toupper(Country),
    
    # Genre NA pour tout autre que F et M
    Gender = if_else(Gender %in% c("F", "M"), Gender, NA_character_),
    
    # Correction salaire
    Salary = if_else(Salary < 10000, Salary * 10, Salary),
    
    # Conversion dates (adapter le format si nécessaire %m/%d/%Y)
    Birth_Date = dmy(Birth_Date),
    Hire_Date = dmy(Hire_Date),
    
    # Embauche avant 1974 -> NA
    Hire_Date = if_else(year(Hire_Date) < 1974, as.Date(NA), Hire_Date),
    
    # Identifiant manquant
    Employee_ID = if_else(is.na(Employee_ID), max(Employee_ID, na.rm = TRUE) + 1, Employee_ID),
    
    # Nouvelles colonnes (années révolues au 31/12/2007 pour anciennete)
    age_embauche = year(Hire_Date) - year(Birth_Date),
    anciennete = as.numeric(difftime(as.Date("2007-12-31"), Hire_Date, units = "days")) / 365.25
  )
summary(emp_propre)
emp_propre
```
